scaffolding.note: Scaled with exterior wall area (scaffold.js): about £800 for a terrace, £1,240 for a semi, £1,800 for a detached house, ex VAT. Set 6 October 2026 against 2026 UK guides (Checkatrade scaffolding guide Feb 2026: terrace £800, semi £875, detached £1,200 a month; Homebuilding & Renovating: £1,000–£1,800 for a 3-bed semi; MyBuilder £1,500–£3,000 full wrap). scaffoldingCost stays as the base and the fallback.

roofStripNote: Stripping and disposing of the old roof covering, per m² of roof, ex VAT (6 October 2026). The guides price it separately at £1,000–£2,500 a job (Checkatrade roof replacement guide, Mar 2026; MyBuilder) or about £950 plus skips (Rated People); £20/m² gives £760–£1,980 across a terrace to a detached house.

wholeHouse.note: Indicative finish prices for exploring options. The visualiser prices your actual choices from our sourced catalogue.
wholeHouse.internalNote: Estimated illustrative finish prices, CSS textures only (no photos) — not the real quote. Two things worth knowing: 'White Render' and 'Cream Render' here (£45/m²) are close to but different from the real Alabaster render swatch already priced at £50/m² in the cladding catalogue above, and 'Brick Slips' here (£85/m² of wall area) is a different product and unit than 'Brick Slip' in the Roofline & Cladding tab (£110 per linear metre of trim). Use the real cladding/roof/trim visualizer for a sourced quote.
wholeHouse.roofAreaFromWallNote: Roof slope area as a share of exterior wall area: 0.76 since 6 October 2026, was 0.55. 0.55 had no source and gave a semi 47 m² of roof; the 2026 guides price a 3-bed semi on 64–65 m² (Checkatrade roof replacement guide, Mar 2026: 64 m²; Homebuilding & Renovating, Sep 2025: 65 m²). 0.76 gives a terrace 38, a semi 65 and a detached house 99 m², against the guides’ ~40 / 64–65 / ~95–100, and still scales with the wall area the photo measures. One ratio for the visualiser and the cost guides, so they cannot quote different roofs for the same house. Taken from published guides, so still UNSOURCED against measured roofs: see notes/roof-area-needs-a-source.md.

conservatories.note: Broad guide ranges to help compare styles. A conservatory is priced on size, glazing, groundworks and access.

styles.name: Edwardian
styles.description: Clean rectangular footprint maximising usable floor space. Timeless flat-fronted elevation with strong symmetry.

styles.name: Victorian
styles.description: Iconic faceted bay front adding character and wide-angle views. The classic UK conservatory silhouette.
cons: More complex roof, higher cost than a simple rectangle

styles.name: Lean-to
styles.description: Simple single-pitch roof leaning against the house. Lowest height, ideal for restricted spaces and contemporary bungalows.

styles.name: Gable
styles.description: High gable front with a full-height triangular frame. Cathedral-like feel, with the most light and volume of the simpler styles.
cons: Needs sufficient wall height/space to suit the proportions

styles.name: P-shaped
styles.description: Combines a lean-to and Victorian bay to wrap around a corner. Creates two distinct living zones in one structure.

styles.name: T-shaped
styles.description: A central projection creates a symmetrical T shape, with a dramatic central avenue and wings either side.

styles.name: Orangery
styles.description: Brick or stone pillars with a flat perimeter roof and a central roof lantern. A luxury solid-roof hybrid between an extension and a conservatory.
pros: Better year-round insulation than an all-glass roof
cons: Less roof glazing than a full glass-roof style

styles.name: Garden Room
styles.description: Fully tiled, lightweight roof with bi-fold doors across the front. A true year-round room that feels like a proper extension.
pros: Feels like a real room, not a conservatory
cons: Least roof glazing/natural light of the 8 styles

conservatories.internalNote: ESTIMATED placeholder price ranges — unlike cladding/roof/trim above, these are NOT sourced from any real production data. Replace with real supplier/installer pricing whenever you have it.

glazing.note: Guide prices for supply and fitting, per window and per door, including access and VAT.
glazing.internalNote: Door and window rates are settled prices from the owner's nearly 25 years selling for a national installer, confirmed 6 August 2026: they sit at the cheaper national installer's settled level, about 35-40% below Anglian settled (list less 40%). Deliberately so. Not a supplier rate card, which is why `sourced` is still false. See notes/glazing-rates-from-the-trade.md.
glazing.source: Prices are what jobs settle at, from 24 years selling for a national installer, inclusive of VAT and stored net. The base is close to the keener of the two installers who buy leads here; Anglian settles about 1.6x higher on doors and 2x on a 3 m bifold, which is what the estimate range spans. Checked 2026-08-06 against Anglian list prices less the 40% discount routinely available. Not a supplier rate card. Openers are modelled: openerCost is the net cost of one opening part and typicalOpeners is how many the base rate already assumes, so a fixed light comes down and a three-opener window goes up — see notes/glazing-rates-from-the-trade.md.

windowBands.label: Standard
windowBands.example: 1200 x 1200 — most bedroom and lounge windows

windowBands.label: Extra large
windowBands.example: Picture windows and wide mullioned units

glazing.stylesNote: the founder's settled prices, 30 September 2026, fitted inc VAT, white uPVC, 1200 x 1200 with one opener unless stated: casement £876 (so the standard band is £730 net; the other bands are scaled by the same 730/708 — an assumption, only the standard size was priced), flush casement (one fixed, one opening) £1,190 = 1.36x, sliding sash £2,279 = 2.60x. Bay: a 2.4 m three-sided bay, two openers, poles included, £2,402 = £2,002 net, which is the extra-large band (£1,460) x 1.37. Mike's measurements: 45 / 150 / 45 cm wide, 120 cm high. The bay figure already has its two openers in it, so the opener question is not applied to bays (glazing.js, openerUnits).
glazing.georgianBarNote: Georgian bars, per window, as a multiple of the window price. Our own figure from typical UK trade pricing (bars commonly add about 10-15% to a window), not a supplier rate card; replace when one lands.
glazing.materialsNote: Frame material, windows only. Every window band price is uPVC. Aluminium: the founder's settled price, 30 September 2026 — a 1200 x 1200 aluminium casement, one opener, fitted, £1,904 inc VAT against £876 for the same window in uPVC: 2.174x on the £730 standard band gives exactly £1,904. Colour is included (powder-coated), so the non-white uplift is not added again. This replaces the 29 September 'about 25% more', which was too low. Styles apply on top as for uPVC.
glazing.vatNote: Replacement windows and doors in an existing dwelling are standard-rated. The energy-saving materials relief does not cover them.
glazing.openerNote: Cost of one opening light, net, on top of the band price. The bands assume one opener, which is the common case. Derived from a standard window quoted at £950 with none and £2,247 with two, less the 40% discount: £570 and £1,348 inclusive, so £389 inclusive per opener, £324 net. Flat rather than scaled by band, because an opening light is hardware and frame rather than glass — it costs much the same in a small window as a large one. One measured product; revisit when there are more.
glazing.doorNote: Prices are net; VAT is added at the end. uPVC, composite, double (French) and sliding patio doors are the founder's settled prices, 30 September 2026, fitted inc VAT: uPVC back door £1,498, composite £2,743, French/double doors £2,693, sliding patio £2,090 — stored net (divided by 1.2). On 6 October 2026 Mike took 20% off the uPVC and composite doors as too high: uPVC now £1,199 and composite £2,195 fitted inc VAT (net £999 and £1,829; whole pounds net, so £1 over the exact 20%). The bifolds are unchanged: derived from Anglian's list price less the 40% discount routinely available, divided by 1.6 to bring it to the keener installer. Bifold width rests on two points only — the 2.4 m entry and a 3 m unit at £13,304 list — so anything between them is not modelled and anything above 3 m is not priced.

driveways.note: Driveway planning estimates. Size is told, not measured: a front photograph cannot measure ground seen at an angle.
driveways.source: MyBuilder driveway cost guide (updated 21 Aug 2026); BestBuilders average cost of a new driveway per m² 2026 (reviewed Jul 2026). Where the two differ, the wider range is used. Natural stone blocks £80–£120 (MyBuilder); pattern concrete £90–£140 (BestBuilders).
driveways.internalNote: Per-m² rates are the surface laid. Groundworks (dig out, new sub-base) are added separately because both guides list them as extra (MyBuilder £30–£50/m²). Waste removal from BestBuilders (£250–£700). Dropped kerb and drainage are NOT in the figure; they are named as exclusions. London/SE uplift (20–35%) is not applied, only stated. Whether a quote includes VAT varies by installer — say so, do not claim it. Colour/style does not change the price; only material does. 0054: resurfacing only — the homeowner must say there is a driveway now; a front garden is never drawn or priced (a render invented demolition on number 14). Resin wording strengthened after it rendered as loose gravel twice.

Drainage channels, if your installer finds they are needed (typically £60–£120 a metre)
Prices in London and the South East typically run 20–35% higher
driveways.planning: In England, a new driveway over 5 m² that does not let water soak away (or drain to a lawn or border) needs planning permission. Gravel, resin bound and permeable block paving usually do not. Flats, maisonettes and conservation areas can differ — check with your council.
driveways.noInstallerYet: We don't have a driveway installer in our network yet, so this is a planning estimate only — we won't pass your details on for a driveway.
driveways.stylesSource: Patterns: herringbone recommended for driveways (Beesley & Fildes; Homebuilding & Renovating). Colours: ranges stocked by UK merchants (Marshalls Drivesett Tegula, Bradstone, Stonemarket via Jewson/Travis Perkins/MKM); resin colours from Resin Bonded Aggregates' colour guide; gravel from MKM's driveway gravel guide. No sales-share data found: colours are what is widely stocked, not ranked.
driveways.existingQuestion: Is there a driveway in front of the house now?

existingAnswers.name: Yes — a driveway or parking space
No — a front garden, path or wall

driveways.noDrivewayAdvice: Turning a front garden into a driveway is a different job from resurfacing one: it usually means taking down a wall or fence, a dropped kerb that your council must approve (typically £800–£2,500), and sometimes planning permission. It needs someone to look at it in person, so we don't show it on your photo or price it here.
